note: Doc 24, which fills doc 06's combination table -- specified in the technical spec and never written until now. THREE TIERS, resolved most specific first: an authored pair, then the item's own pool, then the global pool. Doc 24's own instruction is not to add pairs merely to avoid a pool: the fork pool is funnier than forty fork pairs would be, because a pool is a character's relationship to the world rather than to one object.
rule4: Doc 24 note 4. No authored pair may exist without a written line. A combination that should do something and has none is REPORTED as unwritten and never falls through to a pool -- a pool line in place of a missing pair is a gap that looks like content, which is the same silent failure the item-name uniqueness check exists to prevent.

then: Locked. It may check on somebody else tonight.

rules.say: It is locked. I heard it try the door a moment ago, from the inside, and give up.

tuning_fork: I have struck it against it. The fork is still A. The world is unchanged.
That cannot be tuned. I have established this experimentally, which tells you something about my week.
A. Four hundred and forty. Everything else remains as it was.
Nothing. I am beginning to think the fault is not with the fork.
blanket: It is a blanket. It goes over things, or under them, and that is the whole of its range.
I have put a blanket on it. Nothing has improved.
company_map: It is a map. It tells me where things are. It does not do anything to them.
I have held a map against it. We are both embarrassed.
deed: I am not going to wave a legal document at it.
